name: Alcohol
aliases: alcohol, ethanol, ethyl alcohol, ethanol of agricultural origin, alcohol etílico, alcohol de origen agrícola
what_is: Alcohol on a label is ethanol. It may be added to the food itself, or used as a solvent to carry the flavourings. In the ingredient list it may say alcohol, ethanol or ethyl alcohol.
why_botia: Alcohol is forbidden in Islamic law, so if the label declares it there is nothing to weigh up: it is Haram, not Mushbooh. WHO states that no safe level of alcohol consumption can be established where cancer risk is concerned. Even small amounts raise the risk, breast cancer included.
can_1: Detect explicitly declared alcohol, ethanol, ethyl alcohol and closely related label terms.
can_2: Show the Woman and Muslim information layers when alcohol is declared on the label.
cannot_1: Determine the amount of ethanol present or an individual's cancer risk from the ingredient declaration alone.
cannot_2: Infer undeclared alcohol, interpret religious doctrine or advise a person whether they should consume a product.

sources.label: WHO — No safe level of alcohol consumption for cancer (2023)
IARC — Alcohol consumption and breast cancer

title: Alcohol
description: Alcohol on a label is ethanol, added to the food or used to carry flavourings. WHO states that no safe level of alcohol consumption can be established for cancer risk, breast cancer included. BOTIA classifies a declared alcohol ingredient as Haram.
